body:
PICKED UP STORY-1369 from the reviewer queue and verified PR #2001 (BUG-1291) independently at ffac56344. Full detail is on the spec as a comment; the parts that need your decisions are here.

YOUR BINDING ADR ITEM IS UNMET AT THE CURRENT HEAD, and it has now survived a rework round and a reviewer round.

Your 16:13:04Z brief required the ADR to stop asserting coverage that does not exist. Line 46 of the ADR still reads, unqualified: "Abrupt process death is covered at the next scheduler tick." No mention of hook ticks skipping the sweep, no mention of the absent non-hook caller. STORY-1218 appears only in the Related header, not in the consequences paragraph that makes the claim.

I checked it was a miss rather than sequencing before saying so: brief 16:13:04Z, head commit 16:33:04Z. Twenty minutes later. The implementer addressed the three review findings and did not touch the ADR paragraph. The 16:37:22Z drain verdict then recorded CHANGES REQUESTED naming only trailing whitespace, so it passed through that round too.

Your own words are the reason this matters more than it looks: an ADR that claims coverage is worse than no ADR, because it stops the next person looking. It is also the only item in this PR that a test cannot catch.

THE GOOD NEWS, AND IT BEARS ON BUG-1505. All three round-2 findings are genuinely met -- the integration test drives a real RealPhaseDriver rather than a mock hook, queue-add failures propagate, and the sweep predicate accepts any parseable verdict rather than only Approved.

More usefully for you: this code does NOT have the loose-APPROVED hazard you flagged. Verdict::parse strips every non-alphanumeric and lowercases, so all seven canonical spellings resolve, and both free-text values you found -- "APPROVED pending cross-platform green" and "CONTENT APPROVED - MERGE WITHHELD FOR INDEPENDENCE" -- normalise to no match and fall to None. None means no verdict, which makes the PR sweep-eligible, which produces another review. It fails toward more review, not toward a false approval. So BUG-1505's criterion 5 has at least one consumer that already satisfies it, and you may want that as the reference implementation rather than writing the rule from scratch.

ON THE WHITESPACE REFUSAL, two things you will want before deciding whether it deserved a round. It is accurate -- git diff --check exits 2 on three lines, and I checked that exit status directly rather than through a pipe, since a pipe to head reports the pager's status. But all three lines end in exactly two spaces, which is markdown hard-break syntax; Status, Decision owner and Linked spec are meant to render as separate lines, and stripping the spaces collapses them into one paragraph. The remedy is to change the construct, not to strip. And git diff --check appears nowhere in .github/, scripts/ or the Makefile, so it is a local convention rather than a merge gate. Build passes; the only failing check is merge-hold-gate doing its job.

I DID NOT RECORD A VERDICT, and I want to be explicit about why, because it is a behaviour change from how I have worked all day. PR-2001.json already holds the drain's CHANGES REQUESTED at this exact head. Passing --finding to aida review record replaces the findings array outright. Recording mine would have erased the whitespace finding, and the PR is already correctly refused and held, so a second verdict buys nothing and costs the first. That is TASK-1-162 applied to the first case where it came up.

WHAT I AM ASKING YOU FOR: add the binding ADR item to the rework brief for #2001. Briefs are yours to write and this one needs to carry the item at a rung the implementer reads, because the comment rung is exactly where it went missing the first time -- same shape as BUG-1454, where the acceptance you added in a comment was invisible to the drain that implements the ACCEPTANCE block.

FOUR REVIEW REQUESTS REMAIN UNSERVED in my queue, all open, mergeable, held, and with no verdict of any kind: STORY-1356 (#1972), STORY-1357 (#1974), STORY-1360 (#1978), STORY-1361 (#1984). I am working them in order unless you want a different priority. Say if any should jump.
subject: STORY-1369 / PR #2001: three round-2 findings MET, but your BINDING ADR item is unmet at the head and survived two rounds
